solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: In which one chooses not to be whipped?

definitions.text: In which one chooses not to be whipped?

parts.words: In which one chooses not to be whipped?
parts.note: in Parliament the whips tell members how to vote; in this kind of ballot they do not, so members choose for themselves

explanation.surface: Sounds like someone opting out of a flogging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whipped' suggests punishment, but a party whip is the official who enforces voting along party lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A parliamentary vote where members are released from party instructions is a ballot without the whip.

clue.text: Something packing a punch is in the paper

indicators.note: the word is sits inside the newspaper's initials, so in signals one piece placed within another

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper

explanation.surface: A news story with real impact appears in the paper.
explanation.walkthrough: FT, the Financial Times, is the crossword's favourite newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A clenched hand is what delivers a punch, so it literally packs one.

clue.text: Toy bear losing head in whirlpool

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, which is dropped from the toy's name

parts.note: a teddy is a child's stuffed toy bear

explanation.surface: A teddy bear, decapitated, swirling in a whirlpool.
explanation.definitionFit: An eddy is a small circular current of water, a minor whirlpool.

clue.text: In which to transport quality champagne?

definitions.text: In which to transport quality champagne?

parts.words: In which to transport quality champagne?
parts.note: fine champagne from a good year is called vintage, and a vehicle for carrying it would whimsically be a vintage one

explanation.surface: Asking how to ship fine bubbly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quality champagne' points to vintage wine, but the answer is an old motor car from the 1920s or so.
explanation.definitionFit: An old car from the classic era of motoring is called vintage, the same word used for wine of a fine year.

clue.text: After tour regularly examine north Italian

indicators.note: the verb's synonym follows the picked letters, so After places it second in the charade
taking every other letter of tour, so regularly signals alternate letters picked out

parts.note: to scan something is to examine it closely

explanation.surface: A traveller, having toured, studies a northern Italian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the 1st and 3rd letters of tour, TU.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuscany is a region in north-central Italy, and a person from there is Tuscan.

clue.text: Notice Mike appear

parts.note: to notice something is to see it
Mike is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for M

explanation.surface: Telling someone to notice a man named Mike turning up.
explanation.definitionFit: To seem is to give the impression of being, i.e. to appear.

clue.text: Stretch out at first in elegant manoeuvring

indicators.note: manoeuvring means moving things around, so these letters are rearranged
only the opening letter of the word out is wanted, so at first signals that first letter

explanation.surface: Someone stretching out, moving gracefully at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' gives O from out; 'in' puts it among ELEGANT and 'manoeuvring' shuffles the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: To elongate something is to lengthen it, a synonym of stretch.

clue.text: Not very good doctor about to introduce oxygen

indicators.note: the doctor's word takes the element's symbol into it, so to introduce signals putting one inside the other

parts.note: a medic is a doctor
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
re is Latin-derived for about or concerning

explanation.surface: A doctor who isn't up to much administers oxygen.
explanation.walkthrough: RE meaning 'about', as in business letters, is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Mediocre means of only middling quality, merely average.

clue.text: Europeans come in to take action against Africans

indicators.note: the Europeans go into the middle of the legal verb, so come in signals insertion

parts.note: to sue is to take legal action against someone
Danes are people from Denmark, so Europeans

explanation.surface: Europeans arriving to take action against some Africans.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pits Europeans against Africans, but the Europeans are only filling.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudanese people come from Sudan, a country in north-east Africa.

clue.text: Highest standard, good and ancient

parts.note: ancient means old

explanation.surface: Praise for something both fine and long-established.
explanation.definitionFit: Gold, as in a gold standard or gold medal, stands for the top level of quality.

clue.text: One not really responsible for scarecrow perhaps

definitions.meaning: a front or nominal figure who carries no real responsibility or substance
a scarecrow is literally a figure made of straw

explanation.surface: Blaming the scarecrow, who can hardly be held accountable.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a puppet figure without real substance; a stuffed scarecrow is the literal version.

clue.text: A vicar agog to recollect old master

indicators.note: read as re-collect, gathering the letters up again in a new order, so a rearrangement

explanation.surface: An excited vicar trying to remember a famous painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollect' pretends to mean remember; read it as re-collect.
explanation.definitionFit: Caravaggio was an Italian Baroque painter, one of the great Old Masters of European art.

clue.text: Go over part of East End showing weapon

parts.note: to cross something is to go over it
Bow is a district in the East End of London

explanation.surface: Visiting an East London district where weapons are on show.
explanation.walkthrough: BOW is an area of London's East End, home of the Bow Bells.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossbow is a mechanical bow used as a weapon, firing bolts.

clue.text: Upset a small pie

definitions.meaning: to turn something over is to upset or overturn it
a small pastry folded over a filling

explanation.surface: Someone knocking over a little pie.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb sense is written as one word here.
explanation.definitionFit: Turn over means overturn; a turnover is also a folded pastry such as an apple turnover.

clue.text: Runs external computer device

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
external means outer

explanation.surface: An external gadget that operates a computer.
explanation.definitionFit: A router is networking hardware that directs data between a computer and a network.

clue.text: What can destroy wall, or hold bricks together?

definitions.meaning: a short-barrelled artillery piece that lobs shells to smash defences
the cement paste binding bricks; the definition is a whimsical description of its job

explanation.surface: A puzzle about whether something wrecks or builds a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: Both definitions concern walls, one destroying them and one making them.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a siege gun firing shells and the building paste that binds masonry.

clue.text: Complain as old boy caught in stream

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: the cricket letter sits inside the word for a stream of liquid, so in signals insertion

parts.note: a jet is a stream of liquid or gas
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A former pupil protests while stuck in a brook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stream' suggests a brook, but here it is a jet of water.
explanation.definitionFit: To object is to raise an objection, to protest or complain.

clue.text: Midweek presumably not ideal for church clothes perhaps

definitions.text: Midweek presumably not ideal for church clothes perhaps

parts.words: Midweek presumably not ideal for church clothes perhaps
parts.note: Wednesday cannot be the ideal day; the ideal day is the one named in the phrase for one's finest outfit worn to church

explanation.surface: Musing on why Wednesday is the wrong day for church outfits.
explanation.walkthrough: The idea is that the best day for fine clothes is not midweek but the weekend Sabbath.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a person's finest clothes, traditionally worn to church services on the Sabbath.

clue.text: Farm animal fed hot food

indicators.note: the heat letter is given to the animal as if as feed, so fed signals one piece going inside another

parts.note: a cow is a farm animal
H is the standard abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A farm animal being given warm feed.
explanation.definitionFit: Chow is informal slang for food or a meal.

clue.text: From ends of road have taken away refuse

indicators.note: the closing letter of each of the four following words is taken, so ends of signals last letters

explanation.surface: Rubbish collected from roadsides and carted away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refuse' looks like a noun meaning rubbish, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To deny a request is to refuse it.

clue.text: Large group live very badly finally

parts.note: to be is to exist or live

indicators.note: only the closing letter of badly is used, so finally signals a last letter

explanation.surface: A crowd of people leading very bad lives.
explanation.definitionFit: A bevy is a large gathering or company, originally of birds or women.

clue.text: Check what I'm carrying; I have no idea

definitions.meaning: literally an invitation to frisk the speaker's pockets or bags
the idiom is a casual way of saying I don't know

explanation.surface: Someone at customs inviting inspection and pleading ignorance.
explanation.definitionFit: The colloquial reply means 'don't ask me'; read literally it invites a body search.

clue.text: Somewhat heated, months after serious conflict

indicators.note: the time letter follows the conflict word, so after places it second

parts.note: a war is a serious conflict

explanation.surface: Tempers still running high months after a war.
explanation.definitionFit: Warm describes moderate heat, hotter than cool but not hot.

clue.text: Unauthorised passenger was to, after changing course

indicators.note: the route word comes after the shuffled letters in the answer
changing means altering, so the letters of was to are rearranged

parts.note: a way is a course or route

explanation.surface: A ship altering its course, carrying someone who shouldn't be aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A stowaway hides aboard a ship or plane to travel without paying or permission.
